cards.text: Balak, king of Moab, wants Israel cursed, so he sent for Balaam son of Beor to do it. Now Balaam is finally on his way. Balak hears he's coming and goes out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, the very edge of his territory.

cards.question: Balak finally comes face to face with Balaam at the border. What's the first thing Balak says to him?

answers.text: He asks why Balaam didn't come sooner
He thanks Balaam for the long trip
He asks Balaam to bless his kingdom

cards.text: Then Balak adds, “Am I really not able to reward you richly?” Friend, that's a man waving his wallet around like somebody doubted he had one.

cards.question: Balaam tells Balak, “See, I have come to you,” and then asks, “but can I say just anything?” What does Balaam say he must do?

answers.text: Speak only the word God gives him
Speak only once he has been paid
Speak only to the king in private

cards.text: So Balaam goes with Balak to Kiriath-huzoth. Balak sacrifices cattle and sheep and gives portions to Balaam and the princes who are with him.

cards.question: The next morning, Balak brings Balaam up to Bamoth-baal. What can be seen from up there?

answers.text: The walls of the city of Jericho

cards.text: Then Balaam tells Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.” Seven, seven and SEVEN, friend, that's not a favor, that's a work order.

cards.question: Balak argues with Balaam about building all seven altars.

cards.text: So Balak and Balaam offer a bull and a ram on each altar. Then Balaam tells Balak to stay by his burnt offering while he goes off alone.

cards.question: Balaam is leaving Balak back at the altars. What does Balaam say he's hoping for?

answers.text: That the LORD will meet with him
That Israel will move its camp
That Balak will add more silver

cards.text: Balaam goes off to a barren height, and God meets with him. Balaam opens with a report: seven altars, a bull and a ram on each one.

cards.question: The LORD puts a ___ in Balaam's mouth and sends him back to Balak.

cards.text: Balaam heads back, and there's Balak, standing by his burnt offering with all the princes of Moab. Every eye on Balaam, like a whole group chat staring at the typing dots.
Then Balaam lifts up an oracle. He starts by telling what Balak brought him from Aram to do: come, curse Jacob, denounce Israel.

cards.question: In his oracle, Balaam asks how he can curse the people ___ has not cursed.

cards.text: From the rocky cliffs, Balaam watches them. He says, “Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.”

cards.question: In his oracle, Balaam says no one can count even a fourth of Israel.
Balaam ends his oracle about Israel with a wish for himself. What is it?

answers.text: To die the death of the righteous
To be paid the reward of a king
To go home to Aram in peace

cards.text: Then Balak turns to Balaam: he brought him here to curse his enemies, and Balaam has only blessed them! Friend, that's hiring a man to roast your rival at the office party, and he gives the sweetest speech in the building.

cards.question: When Balak complains, Balaam apologizes and promises him a curse next time.

cards.text: One blessing in, and Balak, king of Moab, is not giving up. He asks Balaam to come to another place where he'll only see the outskirts of Israel's camp, not all of them, and curse them from there.

cards.question: Balak wants a new view of Israel's camp. Where does he take Balaam this time?

cards.text: In the field of Zophim, Balak builds seven altars and offers a bull and a ram on each. That's me when a batch comes out wrong: same recipe, new oven, LET'S GO.

cards.question: This time, Balak goes along with Balaam to meet the LORD.

cards.text: The LORD meets with Balaam and puts a message in his mouth again. Balaam comes back to Balak and the princes, and Balak asks, “What did the LORD say?”

Balaam lifts up a second oracle, aimed right at Balak: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.” Friend, when somebody calls you by your full name and tells you to listen, that conversation is NOT going your way.

cards.question: In his second oracle, Balaam says God is not a man. What's his point?

answers.text: God does not lie or change His mind
God cannot be seen by any people
God only speaks through His prophets

cards.question: Balaam says that when God makes a promise, He fulfills it.
God doesn't change His mind. So what does Balaam say about the blessing God gave Israel?

answers.text: It runs out after a year

cards.text: Balaam says God sees no disaster and no trouble for Israel. “The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of the King is among them.”

cards.question: Balaam says God brought Israel out of ___ with strength.

cards.text: And not just any strength. Strength like a wild ox. Then Balaam turns to the subject of spells and divination.

cards.question: Balaam says the right spell could still work against Israel.

cards.text: No spell against Jacob, no divination against Israel. Balaam says it will now be said of Jacob and Israel, “What great things God has done!”

cards.question: Balaam closes his second oracle with a picture of Israel's people rising up. What does he compare them to?

cards.text: Two oracles, two blessings, and Balak is zero for two on curses. So Balak, king of Moab, comes at Balaam with a brand new demand.

cards.question: Balak now tells Balaam not to curse Israel at all and not to bless them at all.
Balak wants Balaam to say nothing. Balaam answers that whatever the ___ says, he must do.

cards.text: Balak still won't quit, and now he's walking Balaam to a THIRD spot, like me carrying my phone all over the bakery hunting for one more bar of signal. He tells Balaam, “Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”

cards.question: For spot number three, where does Balak take Balaam?

cards.text: Up on Peor, looking out over the wasteland, Balaam says that line again: “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”

cards.question: At Peor, Balak refuses to build any more altars.

cards.text: Seven more altars on Peor, and Balak has now built more altars than I own mixing bowls. We're pausing right here, friend, but this mountaintop isn't finished with us yet.
